## 2026-09-16 restart: applying the follow-up review's findings

A restarted agent found all four findings of the follow-up review already implemented in the working tree from a prior attempt (verified by reading each file, not by trusting this note):
- src/Wakeel.Design/wwwroot/js/app.js: `setInputValue`'s stale-write guard already reads `el.value !== expected && el.value !== value` (the medium finding's exact prescribed fix) — a bound field's Blazor-formatted value is accepted, not just the raw pre-format text.
- src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/VaultStore.cs: `Write` already wraps the stream write + `File.Move` in try/catch and deletes the `.tmp` on failure; `ActivationService.RollBack` already deletes `VaultFilePath(hash) + ".tmp"` alongside `VaultStore.Delete(hash)` for every collected hash; the walkthrough test already asserts the `.tmp` is gone after a rollback (FirstRunWalkthroughTests.cs:433).
- src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/RecoveryService.cs: `CountWrongCode` already resets `_lastCountedCode` when `_login.Profile().FailedAttempts == 0`; FirstRunWalkthroughTests.cs (~line 530-551) already covers "wrong code, successful password sign-in resets, same wrong code counts again".
- tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/FirstRun/FirstRunScreenContext.cs: `FixedTime.CreateTimer` already returns a `ManualTimer` (`LastTimer`/`Fire()`/`Disposed`) instead of falling through to the base TimeProvider; FirstRunGuardTests.cs already has `The_idle_lock_timer_clears_the_lock_out_on_its_own` and `Disposing_the_sign_in_screen_stops_a_still_running_lock_timer` exercising StartLockTimer/CheckLockTimer/Dispose. Wakeel.UI.Tests: 214/214 (212 + these 2).

Ran the exact build/test chain: Desktop build 0/0 -> UI.Tests 214/214 -> Walkthrough.Tests 20/20 (19 + the RecoveryService reset test) -> E2E build 0/0 -> E2E tests.

**New instability found and fixed (not one of the four findings, but blocking a green chain):** tests/Wakeel.E2E/GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs's W08ScreenshotDiff failed intermittently (roughly half of ad-hoc repeated runs, on an otherwise idle machine with no concurrent build) at a perfectly reproducible 33.9672% instead of the ~33.30% baseline. Diagnosed live by diffing a passing and a failing run's actual.png pixel-for-pixel (small standalone System.Drawing tool in the scratchpad, since ImageMagick/Python were unavailable): the difference isolates to the sidebar (WSidebar.razor, `.w-sidebar`), which was still painting a stale colour (dark theme's `--w-sidebar` #0E1519, or the light theme's `--w-sidebar-hover`) at the moment CDP's `Page.captureScreenshot` read the composited frame, even after `document.documentElement`'s `data-theme` attribute and the sidebar's own `getComputedStyle` already reported the correct light, non-hovered state — a compositor-paint race that no synchronous DOM/CSSOM check (however soon after the capture) can observe, since `getComputedStyle` is synchronous with the CSSOM, not with what has actually been painted. Root cause lives in WSidebar.razor / the app's theme-application startup path, both outside this package's allowed paths. Fix applied entirely within tests/Wakeel.E2E/GalleryAndAttentionCenterTests.cs (an allowed path): after navigating to /w08, re-wait for `data-theme === 'light'` (a fresh GotoAsync reboots the whole Blazor app from a themeless static document) and add a fixed 250ms real-time settle (`page.WaitForTimeoutAsync(250)`) before the capture, giving the sidebar's repaint time to actually land. Verified with 12/12 consecutive `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.E2E --no-build` runs passing (zero failures), versus roughly 50% failing before the fix over a comparable sample. This is a timing mitigation, not a guaranteed fix — a future package that touches WSidebar.razor or the theme-application path should look at removing the wait once the underlying race is fixed at the source; the reasoning and the exact race are documented in a comment directly above the `Assert.InRange` in the test.

Full chain re-verified green after this fix: Desktop build 0/0 -> UI.Tests 214/214 -> Walkthrough.Tests 20/20 -> E2E build 0/0 -> E2E tests 4/4.
